text: Staff in these centres should understand the background of the seniors and slowly build bonds with them through various activities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The centres should also coordinate programmes of VWOs and the Government and look after the needs of the elderly at different stages.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think this operating model will greatly simplify the collaboration process and is worth being introduced more widely.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Page: 29 Many professionals are still healthy after retirement and they want to contribute to the society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But, sometimes, just because they do not know how, their passion and skills end up being wasted.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These professionals include retired teachers, nurses, lawyers and accountants.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They possess knowledge, skills and experience accumulated over a life long time and it will be good that there is central system which can act as a middleman, introducing them to organisations that need their service.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: By doing so, these senior volunteers can maximise their time, remain healthy physically and mentally, and stay connected with the society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The benefiting organisations also save money and manpower at the same time.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is killing two birds with one stone.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The problem is that not every HDB block's tenants can help.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As EMSU has 24-hour emergency service, it should also be able to receive emergency signals sent by AAS.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As long as we all do our part, our society will be filled with love and care.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This restructuring is a key part of the Ministry of Communications and Information's (MCI's) policy agenda for this new term of Government.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In his Address, the President said that "we must adapt as the world changes".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Few sectors have changed as much as infocommunications technology (ICT) and media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Infocomm media technologies have fundamentally disrupted established business models.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Today, the biggest taxi company in the world, Uber, does not own a single car.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The largest purveyor of accommodation in the world, Airbnb, owns no hotels or rooms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our motivation to restructure IDA and MDA is to help Singapore seize the opportunities presented by these technological changes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The first, Madam, is convergence – the increasing overlap between ICT and media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We see this in many ways – traditional telecommunications companies (telcos) expanding into content creation, such as StarHub, new media companies delivering content over the Internet, such as our own Viddsee.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 30 In order to better harness the power of convergence, we reviewed our approach towards the development of the infocomm media sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The report showed the many ways in which the media sector was embracing digital technology in order to better understand audiences and create even more appealing content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It also showed how technologies developed for the media could be applied in other settings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Data can be invaluable in allowing service providers to improve the way their services are delivered by making them more customised and anticipatory.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The public sector is also actively looking at ways to use public data to get a better understanding of people's needs and how to meet them in a seamless and cost-effective way.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Those of us who use YouTube will know that it recommends videos based on what we watch and like.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Mediacorp is doing likewise on its online platform, Toggle.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Using data, it will recommend programmes to enhance your viewing pleasure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: More importantly, Mediacorp will also use the data to improve the content that it produces.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One reason there is Big Data is the advent of the Internet of Things.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With declining cost of sensors and cloud storage, it is now possible to connect devices to the Internet and to each other.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Another area is how machines can improve productivity through learning algorithms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One of the major areas that machine intelligence is leading us to is an understanding of natural language voice commands.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We have been using natural language processing (NLP) technology in delivering Government e-services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One of the virtual assistants serving more than one agency is called "Jamie".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Virtual assistants can help to free up scarce manpower to do other important work or building up the most common questions posed which we then use to improve our policies and processes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In future, NLP can provide real time translation for "live" television, benefitting the hearing-impaired.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They can translate languages so viewers can enjoy content produced in foreign languages.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: All these technologies will continue to develop and will only get cheaper, more mature and more reliable over time.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Internet of Things will generate immense pools of data which, through the application of data analytics, will generate fresh insights and offer new possible solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: How we respond to these trends will determine how much benefit we derive from them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We must use technology to benefit our economy and our society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Indeed, there is tremendous potential in pushing the frontiers of technology in various service sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, in healthcare, cognitive systems like IBM's Watson are being trained to analyse medical images and videos and perform diagnoses to a very high accuracy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Developments in remote medical care will allow doctors to consult with their patients, healthcare providers or caregivers without the need to be physically present with their patients.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These technologies will help make the provision of healthcare services more efficient and less manpower-intensive, and support our ageing-in-place initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 31 IMDA will drive further sectoral innovations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We will work with the industry and community to develop these shared solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Next, Madam, we will use the opportunity offered by new technologies to further improve Government services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We have been pioneers in many areas of Government service delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We were one of the first globally to deliver nationwide fibre-to-the-home broadband with the Next Generation Nationwide Broadband Network.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As a government, we have also used technology boldly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We implemented the computerisation of the Civil Service in the 1980s.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We also led the way into cloud computing for Singapore to enable organisations to consume infocomm services without the need to own expensive servers and data centres or operate an IT infrastructure team.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As technology changes and matures, the new GTO will help our Government to understand and use technology boldly to deliver better public services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With an expanded mandate to grow new technology capabilities, GTO will also support the Government in its digital transformation efforts and build engineering talent for the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It will also help public agencies realise the capabilities to build a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We will, hence, see more improvements and initiatives that will bring more benefits to citizens and improve their quality of life.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Infocomm media has tremendous growth potential to contribute to our Singapore economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With a vibrant infocomm media sector, we will see many good jobs that have meaning and purpose and which have good career prospects for Singaporeans to aspire towards.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One such Singaporean is Janice Chan, a layout and match-move artist at Industrial Light and Magic (ILM) Singapore Janice has worked on a number of movies, such as "Transformers", "Hitman: Agent 47" and, of course, "Star Wars: The Force Awakens", and is now working on "The Great Wall", a US$150 million project directed by Zhang Yimou.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: She is one of the many talented Singaporeans putting their mark on global productions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA, Madam, will continue to work with companies, both locally and internationally, to raise the capabilities and profile of our local talent.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I am confident many will bear fruit in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 32 IDA's Infocomm Investments Pte Ltd (IIPL) has invested in a number of accelerators to build high-growth, innovation-driven technology start ups in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IIPL created an incubator space, which they call BASH.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It was set up almost a year ago at Block 79 at Ayer Rajah Crescent.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It has become a home and a place for members and partners of the tech building community across the entire value chain – from accelerators to investors, incubators and entrepreneurs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They gather at BASH to exchange knowledge, co-create innovations and seal deals.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The energy at BASH is quite incredible; we not only see start ups work hard to realise their vision, but also share experiences and help one another to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In fact, I hear that many successful start ups, like Glint and Carousell, keep returning back to BASH to meet more mentors and investors, even though they have officially graduated from our accelerator programmes and moved out since.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will support BASH and more of such spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: And for those who aspire to create great media content for new digital platforms, they can look forward to the Creators' Space, which will be built later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There will also be equally vibrant places for GTO engineers and programmers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The recently opened HIVE has become a fledgling centre of excellence in data analytics, software design and development.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The team has also helped to develop OneService, a one-stop platform which helps agencies resolve issues faced by the public by collating public feedback and routing them to the relevant Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The new IMDA and new GTO will continue to engage the public to co-create solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The hackathon saw more than 300 entries from participants as young as five years old!

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: More recently, I attended the Designathon organised by DesignSingapore Council.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One hundred and seventy participants took part in the 36-hour challenge to come up with design solutions to make lives better for our elderly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One of the teams, Mobilizer, came up with an innovative walking stick to prevent the elderly from falling.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Lee Jung Wei, one of the team members, is serving his National Service.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: He had just booked out of his army camp for the weekend, and, of all the things that he could have done, he chose to come down to the Designathon to work with his friends.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There is a lot of excitement and energy, and it speaks volumes of our young people who want to make Singapore a better place.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In the digital economy, Madam, data will become a new currency of great value both to businesses that use them and the individuals who provide the data.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To maintain the confidence of individuals that their data is being well-managed and is not abused, to develop Singapore's reputation as a mature venue for data and to build up trust in the Singapore economy, we need a balanced and robust data protection framework.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 33 Mdm Speaker, with the new GTO and new IMDA, my hope for the future is that Singapore is at the forefront of technology, with Government departments that use technology boldly, with an economy that is constantly transformed for the better through technology, and with a people comfortable and welcoming of technological change.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: What sort of community and society do we wish to have?

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: How can our community be adaptive and ready for the future?

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: How can the Government and the community build upon our past efforts and co-create solutions to meet new challenges?

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Please allow me to share three challenges ahead for the Malay/Muslim community and how we can work together to chart the way forward.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The first challenge, Madam, comes from a rapidly evolving and volatile modern economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The restructuring of the economy and increasing competition mean that our businesses and workers need be more productive, adaptive and committed to continual upgrading.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Organisations like the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry and MENDAKI SENSE have stepped up to partner national agencies like the Workforce Development Agency (WDA) and Spring Singapore to bring the full range of SkillsFuture support for training and skills mastery.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: But all these efforts will only succeed if members of our community step forward with the desire to learn and equip themselves and if companies actively support and invest in developing their workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Without this commitment, the consequences will be grave.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We may have a pool of well-meaning, hardworking workers, but they lack the skill sets to compete and do well in the new economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The second challenge, Madam, is that of diversity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Malay/Muslim community has always consisted of various ethnicities and schools of Islamic thought.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our community's religious life has always been shaped by the basic principles of moderation, respect for differences, the promotion of inclusiveness, and openness to diversity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We know very well that we cannot afford to be divided by narrow views or the selfish agendas of a few individuals or groups.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Yet, in recent times, we have started to see some quarters in society, and not just in the Malay/Muslim community, holding stronger, if not intractable, views on a range of complex issues.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Harsh judgements and pejorative labels have been unnecessarily passed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Online media trends, migration changes, and regional and global influences, including developments in the Middle East, threaten to accentuate our differences and bring culture wars that are taking place half the world away to our doorstep.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Faced with these challenges, our community needs to continue to stand together to foster an environment of mutual respect and understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, this will be an increasingly difficult job as we try to balance competing views and interests, and as our usual approach of negotiating sensitive matters carefully and discreetly is being challenged.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This brings me to the third challenge, which is that of extremism.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Just as we rose strongly against the challenge of the Jemaah Islamiyah threat more than 10 years ago, we must press on to reach out to every segment of the community and speak with one rational, moderate voice against exclusivist and extremist doctrines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such a time also calls for extra vigilance to keep our country safe and secure, whether against radical ideologies, errant preachers or of any suspicious activities around us.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We must stand as one united people and not let the radical actions of a few spread fear and suspicion among the different communities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We have faced difficult challenges in the past, but, together with the Government, we have been able to tackle them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The positive state-community relationship has been steadily built over the last 50 years, thanks to the support and patience of the community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With that trust and confidence, the Government went beyond national initiatives, such as public housing, education, and healthcare, to also make inroads in areas key to the community's progress and socio-religious life.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This started with the passing of the Administration of Muslim Law Act in 1968 to set up MUIS and to regularise the Syariah Court and the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In 1975, the Government facilitated the introduction of the Mosque Building Fund (MBF) to allow Muslim workers to contribute to the construction, and later also upgrading, of our mosques.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In 1982, we partnered the community to form Yayasan MENDAKI to address the under-achievement of our Malay/Muslim students.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This link between the state and the community has strengthened over the years and allowed the community to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Such state-community engagement on sensitive matters or issues of interest is not unique to the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It has been the Government's approach for other communities as well.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There was some measure of give-and-take during the discussions, with both sides eventually coming to an agreement on the three "live" music points and seven music-transmission points along the route.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Importantly, there was an openness and appreciation of needs and constraints as state and community worked together to arrive at the best possible solution.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: They will evolve with the external environment and as the community progresses.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Also, the perspectives of Government and communities may not always be aligned because we view issues with different concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, the Government may be wary of how rising religiosity could lead to deeper divides, but some followers from the different faiths may see religiosity as a positive development that could 	Page: 35 translate into a more spirited and engaged community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We want to work with the community to realise multiple possibilities and to dabble less in narrow binaries.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: A transactional "winner takes all" relationship between the Government and the community is one-sided and will not be helpful for all parties.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It cannot be as optimal as a relational approach, where both sides are co-creating "win-win" solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These are good initiatives, but we must continue to build on these to develop stronger processes of mutual engagement between state and community that can be sustained for the next 50 years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Differences of views have and will continue to emerge between the two sides.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is how we manage those differences to allow for a greater plurality of views and ideas, and yet not pull the society apart.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is always easier to dismiss differences for its perceived potential divisive effects.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: But it is far more enlightened and progressive to look for ways to accommodate some of the differences in order to enlarge the common ground.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is the best way, and the only way for the Government, as we shape our future together.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is an approach of honesty and mutual understanding, as, together, we will weigh the concerns, weigh the constraints and options for both the Government and the community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Most importantly, it is an approach to work through our differences and enlarge our common ground, as we seek to reach the best solutions possible together.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: But as the President said, "The future of Singapore is what we make of it… everyone plays a part in building our nation".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I have every faith that we will overcome our challenges by standing together.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We are already starting from a much better place than ever before.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our foundations are strong, our institutions are sound, and our people are motivated.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: That Singaporeans have given the new Government a strong mandate only inspires us to keep giving our best for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I am convinced that an even stronger partnership between the community and the Government is, and must be, the way forward to co-create the future.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For the community, let us continue to stay united, to inspire success in one another, and to step forward to lead this community to even greater heights.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Singapore is our home, and, together, we will build this nation for our children and for many generations to come.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Mdm Speaker, for the past 50 years, the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore has achieved remarkable progress.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We made major contributions to the nation as an important partner in the effort to strengthen Singapore's multiracial and multi-religious society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This new term of Parliament is a starting point that provides us with a good opportunity to re-evaluate the type of Malay/Muslim community that we want for our children and grandchildren.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: How can the Malay/Muslim community prepare itself to overcome future challenges?

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Essentially, we want to strengthen the cooperation between the Government and the Malay/Muslim community because this has been the cornerstone of our progress.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This positive cooperation comes from the strong support and perseverance of the Malay/Muslim community, 	Page: 36 who have given their trust and confidence to the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As a result, the Government was able to introduce special supplementary policies that contribute to the progress and well-being of the Malay/Muslim community's socio-religious life.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For instance, the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) was passed in 1968 and has resulted in the establishment of MUIS, the Syariah Court and ROMM.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This positive cooperation between the Government and the community continues to be strengthened year after year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Government's efforts to constantly consult and involve the community closely when dealing with issues have clearly produced results.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is clear that the Government wants to continue working with all Singaporeans, including the Malay/Muslim community, in order to achieve mutually beneficial outcomes, through the process of consultation, information and idea gathering, and cooperating with the people to create the best solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Although it is tough, by virtue of our strong fighting spirit, I am confident that the Malay/Muslim community can overcome these challenges, just as we have successfully done before.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In fact, today, we are in a better position: our foundation is strong, our institutions are stable and our community members are more mature, more qualified and more confident.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: We have a very small domestic economy and must "plug" into the world if we are to do well.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I hope, in my speech, to describe what economists and researchers see as potential changes that will confront us.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Many of my colleagues here have spoken about them and I will reinforce some of those points.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Not all these changes will have a big impact on us, but some definitely will.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: If we are not alert to them, then we risk being left behind.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Going forward, some things will change linearly but probably at a faster clip as technologies from diverse fields advance and converge to produce solutions that were not possible previously.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Other things will face non-linear changes brought about by disruptive technologies, that my colleague Henry Kwek talked about, the way cassette tapes or general cargo ships gave way to the iPod and container ships.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It did not succeed initially because robots then were not dexterous enough and were costly.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Today, many of these shortcomings in robotics have been overcome.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Other companies like Asea Brown Boveri (ABB), a Swiss and Swedish joint venture, are also deep into robotics research and production.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It now produces robots that can be sophisticated enough to do very micro-type circuitry assembly, and at low cost – each robot costs about the price of a car in Sweden, not in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: ABB called their robots "Yumi" which stands for "You and Me (the robot)", collaborating in manufacturing.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: In the early 2000s, manufacturing moved to China in a big way, because environmental laws were less stringent, labour costs were low and labour relations more stable than in the West.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: One would think that China which has to find jobs for a population of 1.4 billion, would not want to adopt automation or robotics.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: But they, the Chinese, know that, if they do not, other countries will.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, their peculiar domestic situation notwithstanding, China is embracing this new technology and, if they are successful, they will leapfrog others who are less nimble.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They do not join unions who go on strikes once in a while.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They do not take sick leave – maybe a couple of days a year for maintenance.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They do not argue with their supervisors about work conditions.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They live in the factories, literally, never once late for work.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This is the type of competition that we can expect to face.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: We will see more robots not just in China but also in North America and Europe where a large chunk of global consumption takes place.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The US economy is about maybe 60% to 70% consumption.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Instead of "off-shoring" manufacturing from the US and Europe to China, the buzz word now is "near-sourcing".

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, production for European consumption will take place maybe in Eastern Europe or Europe itself, and production for the US will take place in Mexico, facilitated by NAFTA.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This "near-sourcing" will become even more pronounced as clean energy in the form of shale gas becomes readily available in the West.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This will impact areas like logistics and supply chain solutions.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Change is not only happening in manufacturing, as I have described, but also in services.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Professional work like accounting and legal services can be performed in lower-cost locations like India or Estonia.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The output is then transmitted through low-cost fibre optics to the US, Europe or Singapore where the customer-facing takes place.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Even research work and the very slick power-point presentations of major consulting firms are now produced in low-cost centres in India and they call them "knowledge centres".

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They like to call it "knowledge on tap" in the consultants' jargon.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Many jobs that were thought to be domestic in nature are becoming tradable.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: In fact, many Singaporeans have haircuts in Johor Bahru.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Robots, labour cost arbitrage and supply chain disruptions are but a few of the changes that are taking place.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: As the Minister talked about, drones, the e-commerce wave – 	Page: 38 Taobao, Carousell, Apple Pay, and we have our own DBS PayLah; and Oculus Rift, the virtual reality that can bring you to face a dinosaur, dive deep into the ocean or go into outer space.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Genome editing will change medicine; 3D printing – I thought they print toys, but I just read that they have printed an electric car; batteries – you have heard of Elon Musk – that will be used at home and they would not look like batteries we are used to, but they may be a painting or a sofa set.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: These batteries will take electricity from the grid at night when the industrial needs are low.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: All these change the way we commute, the way we shop, the way we pay, the way we play, the way we learn and perhaps even the way we think.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Such developments could be viewed as threats but, if we are nimble, they also present Singapore with many new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It is easy to become complacent with past successes or to buckle under political pressure to take it slow, to "relax", so they say.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: And I heard in this House, "Just be happy!" The reason why our economic thinkers in Government are somewhat "paranoid" about economic growth is because we cannot risk a hollowing out of our economy.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The Committee for the Future Economy, led by Minister Heng, has its work cut out.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, is the new SkillsFuture Statutory Board and the Smart Nation initiative.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: If we do all these well, Singaporeans will continue to live good lives.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: As we embark on economic transformation, we also want to avoid the pitfalls of unfettered capitalism.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, in line with such arguments, there are calls to protect our citizenry.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Should our political instincts be "to protect" or "to prepare"?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The programme recognises that the world is changing faster than most people can cope on their own; that learning does not end with formal education, that we all need to learn, unlearn and relearn throughout life, lest our skill sets become less valued or outright irrelevant.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Having said that preparing our workforce is a more enlightened path, I am especially concerned about our professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs).

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I believe they need a little more protection, especially against unfair employment practices.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: We have talked about this, where Singaporean PMETs are sidelined for other nationalities because the bosses from the same other nationality are more comfortable working with their own kind and not because we are less skilled as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This is prevalent in certain sectors of our economy and also in certain companies more than others.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: And, indeed, the space that they occupy and the work that they do are subject to wage arbitrage.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It is, of course, easy to empathise with them to see the 	Page: 39 injustice in unfair employment practices on our own soil.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: We are fortunate to have a Government which is always forward-looking.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: It understands our strengths and vulnerabilities and then charts a course to take the country forward.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Whilst change can be disconcerting and intimidating at times, it also presents many new opportunities, if we stay nimble.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Singapore has more resources than it ever had.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: We can use them to protect the vulnerable groups and prepare the rest of us for what is to come.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I see a Singapore future that is bright and exciting.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Mr Perera bemoans the low number of Opposition Members in this House.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Yet, in the same breadth, he calls for open contests.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: That Singaporeans have voted for the PAP and also six other Opposition Members is the outcome of an open contest.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I hope the Member and his party will respect that outcome.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: We, on our part, are humbled by the outcome and will work even harder to do well for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: On top of that, the PAP Government also introduced the Nominated Member of Parliament scheme, so, like the Member said, different segments of society and their voices can be heard and be represented in this House.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: On that note, since we are all not robots, I propose to suspend the Sitting.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I will take the Chair again at 4.10 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.49 pm until 4.10 pm.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our employment landscape has changed much over the decades.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most workers from my parents' generation held only one job since they started working and served the same company until retirement.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Recently, I witnessed a colleague receiving her 35- year long service award.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many were amazed that it was her first and last job.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These days, it is not surprising for a worker to change jobs four to five times in his career.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some even take on jobs in different industries.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, technological shifts and rapid changes in customer tastes have led to traditional jobs or tried and tested ways of making a living becoming less reliable.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Page: 40 To make sense of the fast moving dynamics and in response to changes on the jobs front, some workers have taken on a new earning option, that is, to freelance.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is fast becoming a viable career option.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many in our midst probably think that it is about having the courage to change course from being a salaried employee to becoming a freelancer.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, having spoken to many of them on why they decided to forgo jobs which provided them with a steady income every month, I am beginning to understand that it is about wanting to break free from becoming accustomed to a previously secure situation and being oblivious to the need to adapt in view of rapid changes.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some look to freelancing to offer variety and scope of roles that their current jobs do not offer them as an employee.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Of course, there are those who enjoy the flexibility and, naturally, prefer not to be bounded by employer-employee arrangements.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For this group, they pick freelancing as their first option.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The types of freelance jobs have also expanded.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have met many who offer services in photography, copywriting, translation, web design, sports coaching, and the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are also websites today that allow a freelance worker to be registered for assignments, connecting them to offers of jobs both locally and overseas.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such one-stop hubs allow free service buyers to have access to a wide pool of talents, both in Singapore and elsewhere, to engage for projects.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Options for those who wish to pursue freelance work have also opened up.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some even see it as a viable long-term career option.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have met former employees who moved out of a stable and regular income job to become their so-called own "bosses".

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some do so at the prime of their careers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And there are those who also started off by holding down a full-time job and taking on freelance projects on a part-time basis.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Gradually, as they become more aware of the market, they moved to become full-time freelancers, bringing their former skills to the marketplace.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some are also learning new skills and offering different skills options.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, there are trainers that I met who also double up as translators.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What used to be popular among stay-at-home mums, retirees and undergraduates looking for some earnings has become more viable and stable.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On society's mindset, many still deem freelancing as a deviation from the norm and equate it to unstable earnings or being more suited for retirees or as a temporary stint.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Since young, we are encouraged to study hard, get the best skills, secure a full-time job, preferably with the best employer in that field.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With economic restructuring, however, companies and jobs could be impacted at short notice, and retrenchment, unfortunately, is an unavoidable outcome for some.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: People lose their jobs when they are unable to adapt or acquire new skills when companies go through major shifts or when product lines get obsolete.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Society, too, needs to move away from the past notion of what is defined as a good job and a stable income.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Page: 41 To many of us, freelancing may look like frontier town.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some of the rules appear unclear and the marketplace seems fraught with uncertainty.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, those who are in freelancing choose how to build their own security, overcome uncertainty and make adjustments, as well as collaborate with one another.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many are also refining their old skills and acquiring new ones to stay relevant, even before the Government announced strategies, such as SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They do not wait for someone else to navigate the path ahead for them.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On our part, we need to change how we perceive freelance work and embrace it as part of the changing employment landscape.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the role of service buyers, companies, we know, are always on the lookout for new ways to do business and to reduce costs.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some, freelancers are a source of talent pool.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With no actual headcount, they can keep costs low, have access to a worldwide pool of talent and are able to obtain services anytime, anywhere.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Perhaps, companies are already making structural changes as to how they assemble the resources needed to complete tasks in this changing environment.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For these companies to work well with freelancers, they do not treat them as a cheaper option.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They make reasonable demands, respect intellectual property and make payment on time for the freelancers' services.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For other companies contemplating the option of using freelancers, it is, therefore, wise to adopt the same approach.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They can only tap on the best services if freelancers are allowed to grow well, earn decently and sustain their businesses.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I propose that high among the service buyers' priorities must be to learn how to tap on the different capabilities out there and treat freelancers fairly to achieve a win-win situation.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On our policies, we have good schemes to help our Singaporean working people.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, some of our schemes and attitudes need to be reviewed to consider the needs of freelancers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our system to help Singaporeans apply for HDB housing and prepare for retirement has worked well for those who hold conventional jobs.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We talked about encouraging an entrepreneurial and pioneering spirit in our people.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is, indeed, a positive sign that there are increasingly more Singaporeans opting for freelance work.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is, therefore, crucial that we offer them the right support that can benefit them directly and enable them to thrive.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This current generation of workers change jobs many times in his career lifespan.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That is how we respond to economic and business shifts.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our next generation of workers will have to tackle a different set of challenges.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Freelancers, like many new working people, are seeking new earning options and it should not surprise us if, one day, our new job entrants' preferred choice of earning comes from freelancing.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Page: 42 Freelancers are responding to the new competition and adopting approaches that we may deem unconventional.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, some of us regard their decisions to discard their well-paying jobs as a bold one.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As the President said, we are embarking on "a new chapter of nation-building".

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Last year, we celebrated half a century of economic progress and success.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This was the product of decades of hard work by our forefathers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will need to have the same resilience and enterprising spirit, in order to write the next chapter of our economic miracle together.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, with the changing population demographics, disruptive technologies and new global economic challenges, the previous formula for economic success may no longer be adequate to ensure our economic resilience for the next 50 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For Singapore to remain competitive, we need to do things differently.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A new formula for success may be required.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our businesses need to go beyond adding value and competing on costs and move on to creating value and competing on innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a significant part of our economy, SMEs play a crucial role in the transformation of our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In Mandarin):  In the last few months, I have met with a number of SMEs and had a deeper understanding of the way they operate.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They almost unanimously highlighted one point: the various challenges that they face today have brought about greater pressure.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Two of the major challenges that our SMEs face are in the areas of manpower and rentals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On the manpower front, the key issues faced are rising manpower costs and difficulties with attracting and retaining talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition, SMEs also have difficulty in coping with rising rents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While there are cyclical factors affecting both issues, they also stem from the fact that Singapore is, fundamentally, a small country with limited resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In order to address manpower challenges, our economy needs to transform and shift towards growth driven by productivity improvements and make the best use of available manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Rental increase is another challenge faced by SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many SMEs have told me that they have been struggling with rising rents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, the Government will do its best by working through the market to ensure that there is enough space supply to meet long-term needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I believe sufficient supply would mitigate the adverse trend of rising rents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At Singapore's current stage of economic development, our companies, particularly SMEs, need to pursue growth through innovation and internationalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With innovative technologies, SMEs can introduce new products and services to consolidate their market position.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By internationalising, SMEs can tap into larger markets to grow their revenue sources.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government has introduced a broad array of programmes to help companies access the financing, infrastructure and expertise that they require in order to succeed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, many SMEs are still unaware of the channels of assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government will, therefore, engage and consult closely with the business community to identify technology trends in each sector and further improve our various assistance programmes provided for companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also further leverage our current SME Centres to provide SMEs with advice on how to transform and innovate their business models.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition, they should also help the SMEs to forge closer ties with public research entities to design specific technological solutions for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The SME Centres can also play an active role in guiding our SMEs to seek for the relevant R&D and technologies they need.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Businesses undergoing transformation can be likened to warriors on a battlefield.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In order to have well-developed muscles, they have to train very hard to build a strong and healthy body.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will not only ensure that they can face the challenges on the battlefield, but also help them withstand the injuries that they may sustain.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Similarly, in order to succeed in the competitive landscapes, companies must continually seek breakthroughs in technology to develop their unique weapons and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The process of transformation of the business can be difficult and painful, much like life-saving surgery.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even businesses which have realised that they need to transform can be daunted by uncertainties and fear of the unknown future.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But we also know that there are many examples of SMEs which have successfully transformed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, I would like to share a few examples, not only to recognise the achievements of these businesses, but also to give you some inspiration.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As long as we maintain an open and innovative spirit, we can overcome any challenge.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It focuses on manufacturing high-quality and cost-effective products.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, as fewer young Singaporeans are willing to work on the production floor, the company faced severe manpower shortages.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In response, Sanwa invested heavily to automate and mechanise its production and quality control processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Factory automation has also helped Sanwa to perform highly repetitive tasks and achieve higher levels of accuracy, reliability and efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition, buyers recognised the higher quality and reliability of its products, resulting in higher sales for Sanwa.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond improving work flow for its existing businesses, Sanwa has also been actively building capabilities to seek out new business opportunities and niches.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Page: 44 Supported by Nanyang Polytechnic and the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), this consortium pools together capabilities of each member firm in developing additive manufacturing solutions for key customers in niche areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Sanwa has shared with me that this collaboration has been successful because members did not see one another as competitors and were willing to share expertise with one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, members acknowledged that the competition was global and that they had to collaborate in order to survive and succeed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am heartened by the spirit of cooperation shown by Sanwa and its partners and hope that more SMEs will embrace this mentality to develop win-win outcomes for the broader industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another example that I would like to share is Skylace Language School.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In terms of scale of operation, resources and finance, it is significantly smaller than that of Sanwa's.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, it has similarly taken the first step to transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This way, not only do students receive instant feedback on their automatically-marked assignments, it also frees teachers up to focus on their main job – teaching.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Skylace is also looking to implement the same technology to automate its administrative functions, such as payroll.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The underlying point of all the examples that I have shared is that all SMEs, regardless of size, have the potential to transform their businesses through technology to address business challenges and open doors to new business opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, I would now like to finish the rest of my speech in English.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond helping established SMEs to transform, we must continue our efforts to support entrepreneurs and build a vibrant startup ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Startups, particularly those with high-growth potential, are an important source of innovation in our economy and help to rejuvenate our business landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today's innovative startups are transforming many aspects of our lives, from the way we travel and the way we shop to the way we live or interact with others.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The use of Facebook, Uber and Airbnb are well-known examples.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over the past years, there have been strong, concerted efforts by the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and many Government agencies to build a vibrant startup ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through the collective efforts of both the startup community and the Government, we now have in place the key building blocks of a successful start-up ecosystem – infrastructure, financing support, community and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, in the past year, JTC Launchpad@One-North was launched as a deliberate effort to create a startup cluster in the One-North area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The response to Launchpad has been good, with occupancy currently at over 90%.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a result of these efforts, the startup scene in Singapore has gained increasing momentum.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our population has also become increasingly entrepreneurial in outlook.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Based on surveys by the Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (GEM), the proportion of our working population actively involved in an entrepreneurial activity increased from 4.9% in 2006 to 11% in 2014.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On my recent visit to JTC LaunchPad@One-North, I was struck by the passion, optimism and can-do spirit of the startups that I met.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Recognising a market gap in the growing e-commerce space within Singapore and the region, ShopBack set out to revolutionise the 	Page: 45 e-commerce landscape by tying up with online merchants to provide cashback to online shoppers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Its young founders, whom I spoke to, were not trained in computer science or computer programming, but that did not stop them from taking the bold step of starting their own company.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Aware of Singapore's unique value proposition as a well-established Asian hub for businesses, with close links to the fast-growing Asian market, ShopBack decided to build a base here in Singapore and use that to target the neighbouring Asian markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Within 18 months of its formation, ShopBack had moved into our neighbouring markets, such as Indonesia and the Philippines, with support and facilitation from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore, while the e-commerce landscape in these countries were still relatively less mature.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, ShopBack has over 400,000 regional users and receives over three orders every minute.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a first-mover in a rapidly growing e-commerce space, ShopBack is well-placed to establish itself as an important link in the e-commerce value chain and ride on the global e-commerce wave.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our SMEs and startups must constantly be on the lookout for new opportunities and not be constrained by our geographical limits, just as how ShopBack has recognised that the global nature of its business, which means that it must internationalise at a very early stage to reach out to a wider customer base.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a very different approach from what a usual brick-and-mortar business like our SMEs, which usually consolidate their local operations and only internationalise at a later stage of their establishment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Clearly, in the case of ShopBack, it was not Government efforts alone that got them started.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In transforming our economy to be future-ready, startups can be a driver of change.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
