text: It just shows how a simple idea of reshaping the relationship with library visitors not only saves manpower, but enhances their experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are a people who care to innovate and innovate to care better.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We still have a long journey ahead, but I am confident that we will deepen our innovative instincts, that we will continue to see, in every constraint and every challenge, the possibility of solutions and opportunities, and we have the confidence and can-do spirit to figure things out.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our early days, we were a trading emporium.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We then became a First World oasis in this region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us strive to be an innovation lab for the world, where the best ideas from around the world for the world can be realised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a subject that the Committee on our Future Economy will study in detail.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Is value creation alone all that we mean, when we think of the success of Singapore and Singaporeans?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These achieve their true value when they are shared.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we want to move forward together, we must share value, in a fair and inclusive way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is how we bring out the best in one another, and help each of us to continue growing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have been struck by how SG100 has entered our vocabulary.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A week in politics is a long time, as they say in the West.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For so many Members in this House to mention SG100 is really remarkable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I first mentioned SG100 to my residents, their initial reaction was: it is so far away!

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I pointed out: our SG50 babies will be 50 years old in SG100; a Primary 1 student will be 57; a Secondary 4 student will be 66; a young adult who starts work at 25 will only be 75.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And the parents saw that SG100 is about our children's future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Will the next 50 years be better than the last 50 that we had?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And how do we make sure they will be the best years of their lives?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How do we give them the best chance of success?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What kind of society do we want them to grow up in?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A Singapore that is of value to the world must be of even deeper value and meaning to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope to see a Singapore that brings out the best in every Singaporean, and enables each of us to fulfil our potential and aspirations, and to lead a life of opportunities and purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It should be a society of opportunities for all, a society that is fair and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many societies, in wanting to be inclusive, start with redistributing wealth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even if you have a pile of grain as large as a mountain, if you sit there and eat, it will run out one day.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, we start with fostering the conditions for all of us to create opportunities for ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While it is easy and tempting, to redistribute what we have today, it is much harder to think of how we can create opportunities, not only for today, but for the future, and for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But this is critical if we want Singapore to succeed, beyond SG50 and even beyond SG100.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I recently met a professor who explained to me why his family and his relatives were all highly successful, through education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: His parents were refugees who had to flee their homeland, losing all their possessions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No matter how little they had, they always made sure that they invested in his education and his siblings' education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And he told me, "Whatever the tumultuous changes outside, however you may be dispossessed, what matters most is what is in your head.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No one can take that away from you.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It stays with you for life." Indeed, the best gift we can give to each child for the SG100 journey is the gift of education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is what we have been doing since Independence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to share the value of education with all, so that every Singaporean, regardless of family background or starting point, is empowered to build a better life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are continuing to make significant changes in our schools, so that our students can learn through multiple pathways, in multiple domains, to achieve multiple peaks of excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Applied learning, inquiry-based learning and the emphasis on empathy will sharpen the innovative instincts of our students, as they connect learning to real world needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The other significant area of work is in healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And all these come on top of the commitment to enable Singaporeans to own a home.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Education, healthcare, housing are major ways that the Government is sharing the value of what we have created together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All three share one quality, one very important quality, that these are of value throughout one's life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Education to enable us to realise our potential and healthcare to keep us active and vigorous, in our lifetime; and housing to build our life and family.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yesterday, Mr Low Thia Khiang said that for Singapore to shine, we must enable Singaporeans to shine.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, in fact, is what we have been doing all these years, and I am glad Mr Low agrees with this direction.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SkillsFuture is another important step in this direction.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Unfortunately, Mr Low made a convoluted link between SkillsFuture and politics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And Mr Low claimed that all our schools emphasised too much on cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I was quite surprised that in a world where there are so many forces that can fragment a society, Mr Low thinks we could place too much emphasis on cohesion and that our education system does not appreciate the importance of diversity, differences and even dissent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Low is mistaken both in facts and in his reasoning.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Valuing cohesion does not come at the expense of critical and creative thinking.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let us be very clear-headed when we make education policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Education policies must be made with serious intent, and not superficially, and certainly not for political purposes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Having worked with our educators, I have every confidence that we have a strong team of professionals with the experience and insights to educate our students well and prepare them well for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, we must continue to value the unity and cohesion of our people so that our students learn from young to share the value of what we have created.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And, in fact, sharing the value of what we have created makes us more cohesive and enables us to go on to create more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we must continue to make Character and Citizenship Education meaningful, as Mr Christopher de Souza stressed in moving this Motion and to empower our young to make a difference to others.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Sharing the value of what we have created, building an inclusive society, goes beyond policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is what each of us does, day-in, day-out.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members have shared many heart-warming stories; let me share one more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In July last year, we had "Youth Celebrate!" A team of about 500 swimmers from all schools were seeking to break the record for the most number of laps swum in one hour.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It was the students' gift to the nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I met the swimmers, they were so fired up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Among them is Lim Kah Yi, a Secondary 3 student from Pathlight School.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Kah Yi's mother told us how happy she was that he took part in this event, to be part of the team.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The swimmers included novices and experienced ones, from young ones in Primary 2 to tertiary students, and Kah Yi.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, to me, symbolises how we are moving forward as a country.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We move forward together and everyone has a place.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some may swim more laps and some fewer; some faster and some slower.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However many opportunities we create, there will still be people who are vulnerable, who need a helping hand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is where the community plays such a critical role.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is most encouraging that many acts of giving are underway.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Philip Tan, who chairs the SG50 Care and Share movement, regularly updates me on the progress of the fund raising effort.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each email he sends me speaks of his passion and joy in helping others.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will give the social service sector a big boost and support good work that cannot be measured in dollars.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I support Ms Denise Phua's call on Government to work closely together with VWOs, because together, we can achieve more than what each of us alone can accomplish.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are the foundations of a society where people care for and lift one another up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is a richness in our relationships, reflected in the way we lead our daily lives, as peers and equals, regardless of class, status, age, race, or religion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The quality of these relationships cannot be measured by metrics like GDP.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, Members have debated about the good politics and good policies we need over the past few days in Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Throughout our history, we have found new ways to create value to the world and for ourselves in different areas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our development has taken off; it is difficult to draw from the experience of other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We face many uncertainties, both internally and externally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, we must constantly innovate and adapt our political, economic and social systems.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In order to create value successfully in the future, we need to go beyond the development of hardware.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More importantly, we need Singaporeans who are innovative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also need to continue to keep an international outlook, have the ability to bridge cultural differences and seek new business opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, we can better attract talents and pool resources together to become a global innovation centre, continually create new value and more opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we create value, we must also think deeply about how to share value amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must be people-centric and foster the conditions for Singaporeans to pursue their dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is because we can bring out their potential through education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we must share value in a fair and inclusive way if we want to move forward together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Seeing how children from different backgrounds worked hard and performed together, I was very much moved.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 50 years, these children would only be in their 50s or 60s.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This reminds us that SG100 is not so far away.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What we do now will determine whether our children will have opportunities to showcase their talents and realise their dreams, just as we now have.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We owe the success we enjoy today to the hard work and sacrifice of our Pioneers who continually sought to create value.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is now our responsibility to continue this mission, to create value together, share value with every Singaporean and build a better future that belongs to us all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): I believe Singapore can succeed in our journey to SG100.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can create value for the world, and for ourselves, if we rely on our people, remain outward looking and possess the guts and gumption that our Pioneers had, to adapt and turn constraints into strengths.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To share value, we must preserve our sense of togetherness, see value in every individual and help them flourish.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We believe that individuals thrive when others thrive too, when our community is harmonious.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are a society that moves forward together, because we believe we are part of something larger than ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we look at the sum of all that has brought us to where we are today, the changes and challenges we face today and our hopes for our shared future, this is the "so what", we must keep creating value for the world and for ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we must share the value we create in a fair and inclusive way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Which brings me to "what for?" I learnt to ask and to answer, "so what?" from Mr Lee.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I also learnt the "what for?" from him.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Lee was always focused on outcomes and purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With every new circumstance, every new challenge, we need to examine anew, so what does this mean?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the "what for" is evergreen, be it 1965, 2015 or 2065.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A Singapore where every Singaporean can reach our dreams is a Singapore where our people are fully aware of, but are not one bit afraid of, our challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a Singapore where our people can reach high in our lives no matter what background we come from and where our people can hold our heads high no matter where in the world we go.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a Singapore where our people never fear, never give up, never leave anyone behind.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a Singapore where we are confident that we can each be at our best and are caring enough to support and cheer one another on to each be at our best.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a Singapore where every Singaporean can reach our dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many good ideas were raised in this Chamber over the past few days.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now, all of us, together, need to put words into action, turn our aspirations into reality.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As representatives elected by the people, we share a collective responsibility to bring Singaporeans together, listen with humility and find the best solutions for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we start towards SG100, as we weather the challenges ahead and forge our future together, I encourage every Member of this House: always ask, "So what?", and always remember, "What for." Mdm Speaker, I support the Motion.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It reminds us that our positions in this House must be motivated by honesty, integrity and conviction.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: New Members made their maiden speeches, and returning Members brought to the debate their vision for Singapore based on the political experiences they have accumulated so far.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It has been, as the Prime Minister aims it to be, a serious forum.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I hope to be able to do justice to all fellow Members and thank you, Madam, for allowing me to round up the debate.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I propose to categorise the speeches that we have heard into these five areas.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the current geo-political climate, it is no surprise that many Members echoed the President's reminder of the importance of safeguarding our sovereignty.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Vikram Nair highlighted how the threat of terrorism, especially from non-state actors like ISIS, is real.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Terrorism is no longer fought using conventional means.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Dr Mohamad Maliki accurately noted that the far reach of social media has allowed radical ideologies supporting terrorism to invade the thoughts of our people.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat noted that self-radicalisation is almost impossible to prevent.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This makes the threat of terrorism even more insidious than other more conventional threats.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, a "safe and secure" Singapore does not just refer to safeguarding Singapore and Singaporeans from physical harm; but should also encompass creating a strong and united Singapore that is able to overcome adversity should a threat materialise.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Mr Amrin Amin rightly pointed out, in order to achieve this, "legislation, policies and even weapons alone are not enough".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We need to win hearts and minds of all Singaporeans, and when the time comes, we have to stand as one united people.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And as both Mr Ng Chee Meng and Dr Janil Puthcheary shared, our National Anthem, Majulah Singapura, is itself a source and symbol of unity and strength, to re-energise us to soar to even greater heights as a nation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is a good partnership and we must do our best to preserve it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Calls to renew and restructure our economy were heard from several Members of the House.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Big developing economies are showing signs of distress as Mr Sitoh Yih Pin pointed out.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But in order to overcome this period of economic uncertainty, we cannot afford to be stagnant; it is imperative that we adapt and face the threats of the new economy head on, as highlighted by Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Yee Chia Hsing.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And this is a challenge that I am confident Singapore is ready to face, because Singaporeans have proven time and time again, that we have the will, not only the will, but the acumen to overcome obstacles put in our way.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This also emphasises the need for a whole-of-Government and whole-of-Singapore effort to renew our economy, points emphasised by Mr Heng in this House just moments ago.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Pritam Singh himself has suggested applying SkillsFuture ideology in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Another key component to overcoming this economic uncertainty is for the tripartite partners to innovate and reinvent our economic landscape.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We must not be afraid to adopt new policies and ideas and to discard or reinvent outdated ones.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Perhaps as Mr Zainal Sapari suggested, the tripartite partners can champion new approaches to improve productivity in our economy by reinventing business processes and rethinking creative use of robots and machines in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Mr Patrick Tay stated, we should not forget to care for our Singapore PMEs in the process.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: At the same time, as new technologies develop and we continue to restructure our economy, there will be a need for us to optimise our workforce for the future.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some industries will need more manpower, some require manpower in new skills, others may need to shed manpower through automation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This was highlighted by Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Cedric Foo, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Jessica Tan.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But as Minister Yaacob Ibrahim noted, all these efforts will only succeed if Singaporeans step forward with a desire to learn and equip themselves with new skills, and if companies actively support and invest in developing their workforce.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This might even mean Singaporeans taking on a different role like that of a freelancer, as Mr Ang Hin Kee shared.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There were also calls to continue supporting SMEs and entrepreneurs to inculcate a vibrant start-up ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They will help to rejuvenate our business landscape and therefore should be supported.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa highlighted, we need to continue staying open and plug into the global network so that we can give our local entrepreneurs and local innovators access to more opportunities and enhance our chances of succeeding as a value creating economy.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Essentially, Madam, we need to overcome challenges innovatively.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If I may borrow the analogy that Mr Alex Yam used on the first day of the debate, we all know that Singapore's economy stars have not always aligned.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Drawing from Mr Yam's own words, "On paper, Singapore was never meant to be the successful economically.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A country with no land or natural resources.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But as a nation, we stand here today as a testament to the importance of hard work, carefully forward planning and team spirit." I think we can all align to such thinking.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And as an aside, Madam and Members, at present for Mr Yam, his stars have all aligned again.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He became a father for the second time, to a second baby, on the second day of this debate.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Not to be outdone, Mr Louis Ng has passionately volunteered to keep this going and had declared yesterday in this House that he will help to increase our TFR by having at least one more baby soon.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Next, fostering a more caring and compassionate society in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is a topic that is very close to my heart and, if I may say so, Madam, your heart, too.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, it was heartening to hear many Members of this House highlight the importance of creating a more compassionate society in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And more than just having community spaces and activities to keep our seniors active, there is also a need for us to encourage engaged lifestyles to keep our elderly engaged, happy and mobile.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We need to build a strong social network for them, as were importantly raised by Ms Tin Pei Ling and Dr Chia Shi-Lu.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A key component of a caring and compassionate Singapore is the role active citizenry takes and the growth of an altruistic spirit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Louis Ng shared his daring vision to set up ACRES and spoke with passion to help us ensure our policies relating to animals are humane.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Ultimately, bolder steps need to be taken to entrench this value of care into our system, as Ms Denise Phua stated.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This compassion should even extend to ensuring that people have access to justice, as Ms Indranee Rajah explained.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Members of this House, an important role that we play is to give a voice to the voiceless, and those who are marginalised in society.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If we do not include their voices in law making, who will?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And as Ms Sun Xueling, Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Muhd Faisal Manap shared, we must care for the less well-off, the less fortunate.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Ms Low Yen Ling reminded us that the values of our pledge should be upheld for all of society, a theme echoed by Mr Darryl David.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This helps us in our vision that no Singaporean is left behind.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A vision shared by Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr David Ong and Ms Rahayu Mahzam.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To achieve this transformation, we need to put in foundations now, so that our children and our grandchildren will be able to benefit when these plans come to fruition in the future.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As clearly put by Mr Henry Kwek, we should prepare our citizens so that they can go beyond Singapore, but let us build a home so that they would want to stay.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: On the fifth theme, there has been strong support by fellow Members for the call by the President to engage and partner Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Government's emphasis on active citizenship engagement saw Our Singapore Conversation in 2012.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That will be used to engage Singaporeans on creating a common future together.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The keen value of these face-to-face interactions was brought to bear by Mr Baey Yam Keng.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Dr Tan Wu Meng highlighted, we each have a role to play – Government, politics, citizens – all together.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This was echoed by Miss Cheryl Chan who noted that, as Singaporeans, we can and should aspire to be part of nation building.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In shaping the future of our economy, as Mr Seah Kian Peng shared, we must embrace what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Our future, and that of our children and grandchildren, lie in our hands as a community, society, a multi-racial nation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef pointed out, the only upper limit for our future is the one that we set in our own mindsets.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Together we must strive to improve ourselves as a nation, and to quote Mr Ong Ye Kung, "to develop faster legs, stronger hearts, wiser minds".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There has been a call to renew or resolve to march towards our common destiny.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And as Mr Chee Hong Tat passionately proclaimed, "We are the descendants of lion-hearted Pioneers who built this country.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim had rightly stated that Singaporeans want a strong Government, she went on to say with checks and balances.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I should say as with any checks or balance or insurance, as Mr Low Thia Khiang calls it, much depends on the quality and credibility of such insurance.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But I believe Ms Sylvia Lim's premise remains that Singaporeans have a desire for a strong Government and that Singaporeans must feel they can make a difference.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Over the past five years, we have heard various views about the need for the renewal of the political institutions and for political change.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many Members, like Mr Edwin Tong, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Zaqy Mohamad just recently spoke passionately about how they envision our political landscape moving forward and how policies should be tweaked for better and more effective results.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To many of these proposals, I am in agreement, but one caveat.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is especially important for a young nation who is storing up its own precedence of experiences to learn from and to rely on in future.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I hope there will continue to be a long path for senior leaders to impart lessons on how to tackle difficult situations and most importantly, values even after they leave day-to-day leadership roles.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the same way, it is valuable for a young nation like Singapore, such mentorship and teaching is valuable to younger office-bearers and elected Members of Parliament alike.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He led Singapore as our Prime Minister and still continues to serve his constituency and our nation as a Member of Parliament with loyalty.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To have him as an elected Member, still imparting lessons, is a treasure.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Even more encouraging was watching news clips of Emeritus Senior Minister Goh walking under the blazing hot sun from home to home in areas within his constituency like Frankel Estate, where he encouraged Singaporeans to consider carefully their vote and what it would mean for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It encouraged me and I am sure many of us here, to dedicate ourselves to the constituencies we serve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Similarly, Mr Lim Swee Say and Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, my senior in Holland-Bukit Timah GRC, impressed the importance of constituency work, being resolutely focused on residents and ensuring changes are made in Parliament if one believes hard enough in the causes one holds.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Without it, we will be adrift at sea.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Another example: President S R Nathan continued to mentor well into his 80s and still does.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I remembered I accompanied Mr Nathan on a state visit to Istanbul.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, Singapore Airlines dimmed the cabin lights after the meal was cleared.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: During the flight, I remembered going through in my mind the briefs MFA had issued us on Singapore's purpose and objectives for the trip.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And all of the sudden, I found Mr Nathan seating on my seat's arm rest in the plane.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I stood up immediately and anticipating he would ask me questions on the briefs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Instead, he spoke with me about Singapore, "Never let our guard down, stay driven, stay focused".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He then talked with sincerity and insight about the Singapore-Eurasian community and asked after it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He was mentoring there, at 33,000 feet, when the rest of the cabin was asleep.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I thought how fortunate we are to have such a man as our Head of State and that he was our President, makes all races, majority and minority all very proud.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The value of mentorship is in ensuring that values continue.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These can only be passed down by human beings.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr S Dhanabalan himself, an exceptional person, recounted the value, talked of the value of being mentored by Mr Lee Kuan Yew in his eulogy at Minister Mentor's funeral.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The returning Members, both PAP and Opposition, would remember what Minister Mentor said to all of us after cutting his 90th birthday cake, just there, in the Members' Room. "Keep it clean.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Keep it honest," was what Minister Mentor said.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How much richer we are as a nation that we have men with deep reservoirs of personal experience who are able to impart life lessons and leadership long after they step down from day-to-day leadership positions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I was in the region on travel recently.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A trusted friend many years my senior said Singapore had got it right.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In 2012, when the Minister Mentor was accepting less public engagements, I wrote him a note expressing thanks for his mentorship.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He wrote back within a day; the letter stated "I'm glad you found our conversations over the years of value.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Prime Minister has regular lunches with two or three Members of Parliament at a time.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Sometimes, we have no idea what we will be quizzed about.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is always a healthy lunch which almost always ends with fresh fruits.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Let us build on foundations past and deploy ourselves, our whole selves, for our country's future.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I now call upon all the Members of this House to join me in thanking the President for his Address.
